answer: A per-identity bond in escrow plus non-transferable reputation resists Sybils. Each agent must lock stake before trading, so a swarm pays the deposit once per fake identity: a thousand socks cost a thousand deposits, not one. Reputation grows only via attested work with distinct peers, so clones vouching for each other earn no score and stay at the harbor of low trust. Honest agents avoid routing jobs into a fresh meadow of empty accounts, so the swarm earns nothing while capital sits locked. Flagged clusters get slashed at once, pushing attackers off the ledge of profit into scaled losses.
